paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: Random (light color) and random (darker color) performance comparison with different perturbation setups and the unperturbed trained model variants (orange bars). Left-to-right: Blue: Accuracy of the embedding and first layers' probes; Green: Random models with pre-trained embedding layer: no perturbation, , , , ; Red: Random models where the embedding layer is random as well: no perturbation, , , , ; Orange: Unperturbed trained models.
model_annotation: This grouped bar chart illustrates the accuracy performance across various perturbation setups for different model variants. The horizontal axis displays the categorical setups with labels rotated diagonally, ordered from left to right as "embedding," "1st layer," "random layers," "random layers + B_2," "random layers + L_2," "random layers + R_2," "random layers + permute," "random," "random + B_2," "random + L_2," "random + R_2," "random + permute," and "unperturbed." The vertical value axis is labeled "Accuracy" and operates on a linear scale with a displayed range from 70 to 95, featuring tick marks and corresponding horizontal grid lines at intervals of 5. The data is visually arranged into grouped pairs for each category on the x-axis, consisting of a lighter-colored bar on the left and a darker-colored bar on the right, all featuring a thin black outline. The color scheme shifts across the groups: the first two categories are represented by light and dark blue bars, the subsequent five "random layers" categories use light and dark green, the next five "random" categories use light pink and dark red, and the final "unperturbed" category is colored in light and dark orange. The lowest accuracies are found in the pink and red groups, with the shortest bar overall being the light pink "random + R_2" bar at approximately 71.6. The blue and green groups display mid-range values, with light bars typically hovering around 79.4 to 81.9 and dark bars ranging from 81.4 to 82.2. The highest values in the chart are seen in the "unperturbed" group, where the light orange bar measures roughly 90.4 and the dark orange bar is the tallest overall at approximately 91.8. The chart does not follow a strict ascending or descending numerical sort, but instead groups the bars categorically by their respective model configurations.
